Ruling 81 (disclosure): one container serves all 70 held-out parents, and it mounts export/ whole, so the graph and the facts of a later held-out parent, which hold the changes of earlier held-out task commits, are readable in it: 54 of the 70 exported held-out histories (export/graphs/

/ancestors.txt) name another held-out parent. The protection against truth from a later parent is per task, not per mount: a task is served only by the model trained on its own parent's graph (s = 1); candidates, comparators and packs are keyed by the task's own parent; and the audit shows for every task that the checkpoint used is its parent (ruling 60), that nothing was folded in (ruling 65) and, through the grader, that the task commit is not in that checkpoint's history (ruling 73). One container per parent is not built.
disclosure81.sibling_seeds: Sibling seeds (disclosure): the held-out rows a run reads are truth-free one by one, but the task rows of one parent together list most of that commit's changed files (item 4). Ranking a task reads only its own row: no code path uses a sibling seed (by_ck groups tasks per checkpoint only to batch them; scoring takes one task's id, seed and candidates).
